text:
jana: ran a sensitivity sweep for algo/proto on the 8xA100 stripe cluster, saw weird non-monotonic all-reduce costs :thinking:
mike: what build + nccl version?
jana: runtime v2.8.1, nccl 2.17.3, single model (bert-base-like) with tensor parallel=2 pipeline=1, batches=8, seq=1024
siva: did you try toggling LL/LL128 channels? that was the obvious first check
jana: yup. LL gave lower latency at small seqs but LL128 suddenly beats at seq>768 for the same batch. weird valley around 800-900 where all-reduce spikes
elaine: can you paste the perf numbers? even coarse ones help
jana: pasted below from perf run 2026-03-11:
```
config: tp=2 pp=1 batch=8 seq=1024 model=bert-ish
LL : avg_step=62.4ms, allreduce=9.8ms, comm/compute overlap ~68%
LL128: avg_step=58.1ms, allreduce=13.2ms, overlap ~80%
seq sweep (700->1100): 700: 59.2ms, 800: 77.5ms, 850: 74.0ms, 900: 79.9ms, 1024: 62.4ms
```
mike: the valley around 800-900 smells like buffer fragmentation / chunking boundary in our proto selection code
siva: agree. If algo/proto selection picks different chunk sizes at that sequence horizon, NVLink bandwidth packing could change leading to poorer utilization
jana: i dug traces (nvprof + our micro-tracer). the all-reduce size jumps by ~40% at 800 because of a change from 128KB chunks -> 192KB chunks in the algorithm selector
elaine: is that coming from our kernel selection logic or NCCL's internal heuristic?
jana: our selector picks algo/proto pair based on message size thresholds (legacy table). NCCL then applies its internal channelization. but the selector decision triggers a different Rendezvous (I think proto switch) so msg size distribution changes
mike: could be hitting an unfavorable prime factor for chunking leading to uneven last-chunk sizes. also reminded me of the small-message padding bug we fixed last year
siva: can we force a consistent proto in the runtime for that range as a mitigation? e.g., force algo=ring/proto=LL for seq <=900 then LL128 after?
jana: did a short run forcing proto=LL128 across the sweep: removed the spike but LL128 worse at seq<750. So we need dynamic rule: prefer LL for <750, LL128 >900, and for 750-900 apply channel-count smoothing fallback
elaine: channel-count smoothing? define that real quick
siva: instead of switching proto abruptly at message-size boundaries, we pick nearest proto but probe alternate proto on 1/16 requests (opportunistic) and measure per-request completion; if alternate is consistently better, ramp it up. keeps a soft transition so we don't get step-changes
mike: implement as heuristic in kernel-selector with rolling 30s success metric. low overhead. Also record per-model histograms in console for that rule
jana: implemented local patch and re-ran: probe reduced the spike amplitude by 70%. sample trace attached in gist: https://internal.gists/redwood/abc123 (private)
infra-bot: deploy note: rolled kernel-selector patch to staging (canary 5% of traffic) at 2026-03-11T14:47:02Z
elaine: nice. did you also check KV cache warmup interplay? sometimes KV cache misses amplify comm work because of longer token prep
jana: good catch — when prefetch window is small (we had default 8), the kernel path moved to a different gather kernel which changed tensor shapes feeding all-reduce -> different chunk sizes. increasing prefetch to 16 stabilized shapes and reduced variance
siva: so two knobs: selector boundaries + kvcache prefetch size. both fairly low-risk to expose as runtime tunables
mike: for rollout plan: 1) keep probe-enabled selector with smoothed transitions 2) bump default kvcache prefetch to 12-16 for TP workloads 3) add perf metric to console: 'proto-swap-rate' + seq-hist heatmap 4) monitor in canary for 48h
jana: created PR #4256 with patch + tests + perf traces in comments
elaine: add a regression eval set with sequences around 700-950 and small batch sizes so CI catches this next time
siva: agree. also add a tiny microbenchmark that reproduces the chunk-size flip in isolation so we can run it in perf CI
mike: awesome. one more ask — document the observed boundary numbers in the kernel-selection README so model-onboarding knows to test these ranges
jana: will update README in PR and ping QA. thanks team :thumbsup:
